source._version_note: v2.15.1 is the latest GA (2026-10-09). go.mod declares `go 1.26.0` and `toolchain go1.26.8`; upstream's .goreleaser.yml builds its releases with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.2 and its v2.15.1 release binary reports go1.27.2, so the builder is golang:1.27.3-bookworm, the latest patch of the line upstream releases with. Under GOTOOLCHAIN=local a toolchain directive older than the local Go is satisfied. No go.work. 2026-10-27, v2.15.2 (2026-10-26): go.mod still declares `go 1.26.0`, now with `toolchain go1.26.10`, and upstream's .goreleaser.yml builds it with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3, the builder's Go.
source._vendor_note: vendor/ is NOT committed (eleven direct modules), so the vendor stage runs `go mod tidy -e && go mod vendor`.
source._build_note: Upstream's release build (.goreleaser.yml): CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, ldflags `-w -X server.gitCommit={{.ShortCommit}} -X server.serverVersion={{.Tag}}`. server/const.go also fills gitCommit from the Go build's vcs.revision (7 characters); this build's tree has no .git, so the commit is stamped.
source.source_date_epoch_provenance: the time release v2.15.3-CE-ubuntu24.04-r4 was cut (2026-11-20T07:52:25Z), by scripts/retarget.py --rev-bump: ReadyStack dates an image by when its release was packaged (owner 2026-11-10), recorded here once and used by every rebuild of the release; it builds upstream commit 2a9066eb57ff, dated 2026-11-11T11:09:33Z (source.commit_epoch).

binaries_from_source.name: nats-server
binaries_from_source._note: Upstream's release ldflags exactly (-w without -s keeps the symbol table, as upstream's binaries do). serverVersion is the tag with its leading v, so `nats-server --version` prints `nats-server: v2.15.1`, as upstream's release binary does; /varz reports the bare VERSION constant (2.15.1) and git_commit (7 characters, b2fd3ef in upstream's binary).
